cf.title: [PATCH] Add parallel instrumentation hooks for CustomScan providers

input.subject: [PATCH] Add RetrieveInstrumentation hook for CustomScan providers

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal, and a reviewer who knows the area accepts it as parity with built-in scans. Three fixable design points remain open from message #13. In v4 the provider picks its own shm_toc key (replication-ondisk-1), a provider cannot print per-worker output as built-in scans do (standards-compat-3), and no in-tree test runs the new path (maintenance-fit-2). The callback signatures should be settled before extensions build against them.

brief.title: Parallel instrumentation callbacks for CustomScan providers
brief.problem: CustomScan providers have no standard way to copy instrumentation from parallel workers to the leader before the DSM segment goes away. So extension authors cannot report per-worker or aggregated metrics in EXPLAIN ANALYZE for parallel custom scans. Built-in scans such as SeqScan and IndexScan got separate instrumentation DSM handling, and CustomScan did not.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds four optional callbacks to CustomExecMethods for estimating, setting up and retrieving instrumentation shared memory. execParallel.c calls them for CustomScanState nodes even when the node is not parallel_aware, like built-in scans do for EXPLAIN ANALYZE. In v4 the provider does the shared memory allocation itself inside the callbacks, and core only checks each callback for NULL.
user_visible_surface: C API: new optional callback EstimateDSMCustomScanInstrumentation in CustomExecMethods.
C API: new optional callback InitializeDSMCustomScanInstrumentation in CustomExecMethods.
C API: new optional callback InitializeWorkerCustomScanInstrumentation in CustomExecMethods.
C API: new optional callback RetrieveInstrumentationCustomScan in CustomExecMethods.
Docs: custom-scan.sgml describes the four callbacks.
author_claims: Existing extensions see no change and no overhead, because each callback is checked for NULL.
The patch follows the same pattern as recent core commits for SeqScan and IndexScan instrumentation.
Tests belong in an extension that implements the callbacks, not in core regression tests.
The patch passes make check-world and is not platform-specific.
brief.thread_state: Tomas Vondra and Dilip Kumar find the idea fine, and Dilip approved v3. Tomas's review of v4 lists open items: core should own the shm_toc allocation and keys, callbacks run without instrumentation requested, test_extensible tests, docs detail, per-worker EXPLAIN access, and callback naming.
unclear: How a provider picks a shm_toc key that does not clash with plan_node_id or other keys.
Whether the callbacks are skipped when EXPLAIN ANALYZE or instrumentation is not requested.
Whether Retrieve runs once at query end or on every rescan, and what it must copy.
How an extension prints per-worker stats while ExplainOpenWorker and ExplainCloseWorker are static in explain.c.
Whether ForeignScan should get the same callbacks in this patch or a separate one.
Which names the callbacks will have in the final version.

prior_attempts.title: asynchronous execution support for Custom Scan
prior_attempts.quote: Since the author or no one else showed interest in taking it forward and the patch had no activity for more than 1 year, I have changed the status to RWF.
prior_attempts.reason: The entry died of inactivity: no one reviewed the patch in depth, and the author did not move it forward. Etsuro Fujita said he would review it once an example extension existed, but the visible messages show no review after that. Vignesh C returned it with feedback after more than a year with no activity.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P2 added asynchronous execution callbacks to CustomScan, and this patch adds parallel instrumentation callbacks. Both extend CustomExecMethods with no in-tree consumer. P2 ended through inactivity, while this entry has an active reviewer who asks for test_extensible coverage in message #13.

objections.title: Provider-chosen shm_toc keys can collide with core keys in the DSM
objections.failure_scenario: A provider calls shm_toc_insert with plan_node_id, or with a constant that another node or extension also uses. The leader stores two entries under one key, or a worker looks one up and gets the wrong chunk. The user sees a crash or wrong EXPLAIN ANALYZE numbers only under parallel plans.
objections.argument: In v4 core only checks each callback for NULL, so the provider does its own shm_toc_allocate and shm_toc_insert. plan_node_id is already taken by the parallel-scan coordinate, and the proposal gives no rule for picking another key. Message #13 raises this as the first open item, and the thread has not settled it. Core-owned allocation, as in ExecCustomScanInitializeDSM, keeps the key-space invariant in one place.
objections.author_must_show: Will core allocate and key the instrumentation chunk, so that a provider only gives a size and fills the memory?

critic.reasoning: In v4 the provider allocates and picks the shm_toc key, and plan_node_id is already taken by the parallel scan chunk. Message #13 item 1 raises this and v4 has no answer, but a new version can move allocation into core.

objections.title: Per-worker EXPLAIN output cannot match built-in format
objections.failure_scenario: A provider retrieves per-worker metrics but cannot call ExplainOpenWorker or ExplainCloseWorker, so it writes its own worker grouping. Tools that parse EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) and expect the standard "Workers" array then miss or misread these metrics. Tool authors find out only when the parallel custom scan output differs from the output of other scans.
objections.argument: The commit message promises that providers can "fully support parallel EXPLAIN ANALYZE metrics" in a way similar to built-in scan nodes. Built-in nodes print worker details through static helpers in explain.c that extensions cannot reach (message #13, item 5). Without an exported helper or a new callback, each provider will invent its own output shape for the same kind of data. The proposal does not yet say which of these two options it takes.
objections.author_must_show: How will a provider print per-worker statistics in the same text and JSON structure that built-in parallel scans use?

critic.reasoning: ExplainOpenWorker and ExplainCloseWorker are static in explain.c, and the commit message promises parity with built-in scans. Message #13 item 5 raises this and no reply answers it yet.

objections.title: No in-tree user, so later executor changes can break this unnoticed
objections.failure_scenario: A later commit reworks parallel instrumentation in execParallel.c, as the recent SeqScan and IndexScan commits did. No core test calls the CustomScan callbacks, so check-world passes. An extension author finds the broken path after the release ships.
objections.argument: Message #1 says tests belong in the extension that uses the callbacks. That leaves core with a path that no buildfarm member exercises. Message #13 points to src/test/modules/test_extensible as the natural place for this test. Without it, whoever commits the patch owns a path that fails silently whenever execParallel.c changes.
objections.author_must_show: Can test_extensible implement all four callbacks and show worker instrumentation in EXPLAIN ANALYZE output?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 puts tests outside core, so no buildfarm member would run the new execParallel.c path. Message #13 item 4 asks for test_extensible coverage and the thread has no reply yet.

refuted.title: CommitFest target "stable" implies an ABI break in CustomExecMethods
refuted.failure_scenario: A provider built against an older minor release defines a static CustomExecMethods that lacks the four new members. After a minor update, execParallel.c reads past the end of that struct, treats leftover bytes as a function pointer, and the leader or a worker crashes during a parallel EXPLAIN ANALYZE. Users find out in production after a routine minor upgrade.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry lists the target version as "stable", but the patch adds members to CustomExecMethods in extensible.h. Providers usually declare this struct as a static constant, so its size is fixed when the extension is compiled. The NULL check the author relies on protects only providers compiled against the new header. In back branches the change is unsafe unless the struct gains a version or size field, which the proposal does not mention.
refuted.author_must_show: Is this patch meant for master only, and if not, how would back branches handle providers compiled against the old CustomExecMethods layout?

critic.reasoning: Nobody in the thread proposes a backpatch, and the entry moved from PG19-Final into the PG20 CommitFests, so the patch targets master. Postgres does not backpatch new extension APIs, so the minor-release crash cannot happen.

refuted.title: Instrumentation callbacks break the existing parallel callback contract
refuted.failure_scenario: A provider author copies the pattern from InitializeDSMCustomScan and calls shm_toc_insert with plan_node_id inside InitializeDSMCustomScanInstrumentation. That key is already in use, so a worker looks up the wrong chunk. The result is a crash or wrong data, and nothing reports the mistake at development time.
refuted.argument: For the existing parallel callbacks, core allocates the chunk, picks the key and passes a pointer to the provider. In v4 the instrumentation callbacks receive only the ParallelContext, so the provider has to allocate and pick a key on its own, and no documented key space exists for that (message #13, item 1). Once extensions ship against this signature, changing it later breaks them. The callback names also mix two schemes (message #13, item 7), so the API is not yet in a state that could be frozen.
refuted.author_must_show: Will v5 change the callbacks so that core allocates the chunk and owns the toc key, and use one naming scheme, as InitializeDSMCustomScan does today?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which states the shm_toc key problem more directly. The naming point is a small item that message #13 already lists.

refuted.title: New CustomExecMethods fields break ABI if backpatched to a stable branch
refuted.failure_scenario: A minor release ships the four new fields. A custom scan extension built against the old headers defines a static CustomExecMethods without them. The patched executor reads past the end of that struct, takes the bytes it finds there as a callback pointer, and crashes the backend on the first parallel query.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry lists the target version as "stable", but the thread never discusses backpatching. Extensions allocate CustomExecMethods themselves, so the struct size is part of the extension ABI. The docs hunk places the new callbacks before ExplainCustomScan, which also shifts that member if the header order follows the docs. On master this is normal major-version churn.
refuted.author_must_show: Is the patch meant for master only, and if not, how do extensions built against older minor releases keep working?

critic.reasoning: Same point as standards-compat-1, and it fails for the same reason: the thread shows no backpatch plan. The objection itself says the change is normal major-version churn on master.

refuted.title: Providers choose shm_toc keys and allocate the instrumentation DSM themselves
refuted.failure_scenario: Two custom scan providers, or one provider plus a core node, insert instrumentation chunks into the same shm_toc under keys they each picked. The plan_node_id key is already taken, so a provider guesses another. A user running EXPLAIN ANALYZE on a parallel plan gets a crash or wrong numbers, and only in some plan shapes.
refuted.argument: In v4 the Estimate, InitializeDSM and InitializeWorker callbacks own the shm_toc allocation and the key, unlike the existing parallel callbacks, where core allocates and inserts under plan_node_id (message #13, item 1). Once this ships, extensions depend on the callback signatures, so moving allocation into core later breaks them. Internal API shape is the part that is hard to change after release.
refuted.author_must_show: Can core own the allocation and key, with the provider only sizing and filling the chunk, as the parallel query callbacks already do?

refuted.title: API may be incomplete: per-worker EXPLAIN output and ForeignScan parity
refuted.failure_scenario: A provider collects per-worker metrics through the new callbacks but cannot print them in the per-worker sections, because ExplainOpenWorker and ExplainCloseWorker are static. A second API change then follows for EXPLAIN, and another for ForeignScan. Extensions must track several changes to CustomExecMethods across releases.
refuted.argument: Message #13 (items 5 and 6) says the main consumer, per-worker EXPLAIN output, may not be possible with v4, and that ForeignScan has the same gap. If CustomScan and ForeignScan get different callback designs one release apart, both need maintenance. Settling the full shape first, including callback naming (item 7), costs less than revising a released API.
refuted.author_must_show: Does a working provider show per-worker stats end to end with v4, and will ForeignScan use the same callback design?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-3 for the per-worker EXPLAIN gap. Message #13 calls ForeignScan "a separate patch", so that part is not a defect of this proposal.

refuted.title: No named custom scan provider shows a need for four new callbacks
refuted.failure_scenario: The four callbacks go into CustomExecMethods and become a stable extension API. No out-of-tree provider uses them, and the first real one finds it still cannot print per-worker stats (message #13, item 5). The project then has to change or add to an API it already promised to keep.
refuted.argument: The thread names no extension, workload or field report that needs parallel custom scan instrumentation. Messages #1 and #3 state the gap in general terms, and the only support is from the author and one reviewer at the same company (message #9). Tomas calls the change reasonable parity with SeqScan and IndexScan (message #5), and the cost falls mostly on providers. But his open items show that no consumer has tested the design yet.
refuted.author_must_show: Which existing custom scan provider needs worker instrumentation today, and why does ShutdownCustomScan, or its own parallel DSM, not cover that case?

critic.reasoning: The leader's ShutdownCustomScan runs before Gather waits for its workers, so it cannot collect their final counters. A committer who knows the area accepts the goal as parity with built-in scans in message #5, and the cost falls only on providers that set the callbacks.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch adds four optional callbacks to CustomExecMethods in extensible.h.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry lists target "stable", but new CustomExecMethods members fit master only.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: execParallel.c gains a CustomScan instrumentation path that no core test runs in v4.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Will core allocate the instrumentation chunk and own its shm_toc key, so that a provider only gives a size and fills the memory?
How will a provider print per-worker statistics in the same text and JSON structure as built-in parallel scans, given that ExplainOpenWorker and ExplainCloseWorker are static?
Can test_extensible implement all four callbacks and show worker instrumentation in EXPLAIN ANALYZE output?
Does core skip the four callbacks when the query does not request instrumentation?
Does RetrieveInstrumentationCustomScan run once at query end or on every rescan, and what must it copy out of shared memory?

committability.owner_note: Tomas Vondra reviewed v4 in message #13. The owner needs to know execParallel.c and the parallel instrumentation code for built-in scans.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the four callback signatures as an extension API for the life of the release, and for keeping the CustomScan path working when execParallel.c changes.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted new versions up to v4 after review and kept the thread alive for nine months. No reply to message #13 is visible yet.

priority.reason: Only authors of parallel custom scan providers gain, and the v4 patch is about 9 KiB in the executor and docs. The burden stays medium until an in-tree test covers the path, and message #13 lists design items a v5 must answer first.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the exact call sites in execParallel.c, the behaviour on rescan and the conditions under which core calls each callback could not be checked. The points from messages #4 to #13 rest on the brief's summary of them.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: asynchronous execution support for Custom Scan
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds asynchronous execution to the Custom Scan API by reusing the approach that Foreign Scan has used since v14. A custom scan provider would start work in CustomScanAsyncRequest, wait on a file descriptor set up in CustomScanAsyncConfigureWait, and receive results in CustomScanAsyncNotify.

Etsuro Fujita said he would review it once an example extension existed, but the visible messages show no review after that. Vignesh C returned it with feedback after more than a year with no activity.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since the author or no one else showed interest in taking it forward
and the patch had no activity for more than 1 year, I have changed the
status to RWF.

precedents_retrieved.title: ctidscan as an example of custom-scan
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds ctidscan, an example custom-scan provider that scans only part of a table when the query has inequality conditions on the ctid system column, with an enable_ctidscan setting. Its main purpose is to serve as sample code and a test for the custom-scan interface, possibly placed in src/test/modules.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane argued that the custom-scan interface cannot support anything of real interest, so a small example like ctidscan does not show that real use cases keep working. He added that the ctid range use case would need less new code as an extension of TidScan. The visible messages end in a broader debate about custom-scan APIs and do not show a separate decision on this patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So a finger
exercise like ctidscan, even though it might have some marginal use,
doesn't do much to alleviate that concern.  It certainly doesn't seem
like it's a suitable placeholder proving that we aren't breaking any
actual use cases for the feature.

precedents_retrieved.title: Free memory allocated by waitonlock_error_callback()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a pfree() in waitonlock_error_callback() for the StringInfo buffer it allocates in ErrorContext. The goal was to stop Valgrind from reporting the memory as definitely lost.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that commit 89d57c1fb had already solved this leak in a more general way. The author confirmed that 89d57c1fb fixed the reported issue and withdrew the patch. Michael Paquier had also noted that errfinish() resets ErrorContext, so the leak was not real.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Didn't 89d57c1fb already solve this in a more
general way?

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove page-read callback from XLogReaderState
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes the page-read callback (and later the open and close segment callbacks) from XLogReaderState. XLogReadRecord becomes a state machine that returns XLREAD_NEED_DATA, and the caller then loads WAL pages itself.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Thomas Munro committed a squashed version in April 2021, and it was later reverted. The author's note mentions a possible defect on one platform but does not give the cause. In September 2021 Thomas Munro pointed the author to a message from Andres Freund that the author had not seen and had not yet answered, and the entry was then returned with feedback. The visible messages do not show the content of that message or the exact reason for the revert.

precedents_retrieved.title: Make it possible to add custom options to EXPLAIN
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Michael Paquier, Pavel Stehule, Andrei Lepikhov
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a generic mechanism that lets extensions register their own EXPLAIN options and per-node instrumentation, shown with a Bloom example and motivated by Neon's PREFETCH option. Extensions register through RegisterCustomInsrumentation from _PG_init, and custom metrics share a fixed 128-byte area in Instrumentation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers raised design problems: the selected flag sits in a global list that nested EXPLAIN ANALYZE can overwrite, the size limit is not needed, and options fail when the extension is not yet loaded. Michael Paquier saw too much maintenance cost next to the existing explain hook. The thread then turned to prefetching, David G. Johnston proposed returning the entry, and a later request for a rebase got no visible reply.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I cannot get really excited about the extra
maintenance this facility would involve compared to the potential
gains, knowing that there's a hook.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support custom authentication methods using hooks
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds hooks in auth.c for the authentication check and for error reporting, and a pg_hba.conf method "custom" with a "provider" option, so extensions can implement authentication. The use case is checking credentials against a central external provider, such as cloud single sign-on, without syncing them into Postgres.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The commitfest manager returned the patch set because it needed author work before more review. Peter Eisentraut asked that extensions register their own method names and that built-in methods such as ldap and pam use the same interface. Stephen Frost voted -1: the hooks cover only the server side, so new methods such as OAuth still need libpq changes, and the goal stayed unclear. He also objected to a synchronous call-out during authentication.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Okay, either way you look at it, this patchset needs author work before any further review can be done.

precedents_retrieved.title: Adding Support for Copy callback functionality on COPY TO api
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a data destination callback to the COPY TO API, matching the data source callback that COPY FROM already has. Extensions could then use COPY TO to send rows to their own destinations, for example for storage, backup or analytics.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author did not answer review feedback for two weeks, so the patch was returned with feedback. The open review points were to run pgindent, to add an in-tree user of the callback, and to have the callback return the number of bytes written and report failure.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This feedback has not been answered after two weeks, so I have marked
the patch as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Xact event callback at command start
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a way for an extension to run code before each SQL statement in a transaction, so that it can implement server-side statement-level rollback. Early versions used hooks around start_xact_command(), later versions used a new XACT_EVENT_COMMAND_START event for xact callbacks, and v5 went back to a hook called after start_xact_command().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund and Tom Lane objected to exposing an API for statement-level rollback in an extension, because top-level transaction state is tied to backend internals and the hook placements would be fragile and add overhead to the exec_* functions in postgres.c. Andres Freund added that a real solution needs core work, such as making subtransactions cheap enough to avoid xid wraparound, and that these hooks do not move toward it. Tom Lane also said the new xact callback events were the wrong design, since they broke postgres_fdw. After this, the author said there was no chance of inclusion and offered to withdraw the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I'm *very* unconvinced it makes sense to implement a feature like this in an extension / that we should expose API for that purpose. To me the top-level transaction state is way too tied to our internals for it to be reasonably dealt with in an extension.

precedents_retrieved.title: Custom storage managers (SMGR), redux
precedents_retrieved.authors: Matthias van de Meent (mmeent), Tristan Partin (tristan957)
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Custom storage managers (SMGR), redux
Threads: Extensible storage manager API - SMGR hook Redux

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent proposed this idea. P8 covers extension EXPLAIN options and its reason, that a hook already exists, does not fit: no existing callback reaches worker data for a CustomScan that is not parallel_aware. P1, P15 and P17 record no reason that applies, and the open design points are already listed in message #13.
The idea itself does not conflict with SQL, pg_dump, psql or GUC conventions. The objections concern the C API contract only.
The patch adds no on-disk, WAL, catalog or wire-protocol state. The only cross-process state is the per-query DSM, which is torn down at query end.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It adds optional C callbacks that only a loaded C extension can set, and loading one already needs superuser. It adds no SQL surface, privilege or user-visible data path, so no unprivileged user gains new access. The shm_toc key clash in message #13 is a crash risk for the provider's own code. That belongs to the design angle.
The idea fits core: it closes a gap left by recent SeqScan and IndexScan commits, and a committer who knows the area is engaged. The objections concern the API shape before release.

ShutdownCustomScan already runs before the parallel DSM segment goes away, and the docs name it for this use. It works only for parallel-aware nodes, though, because InitializeDSMCustomScan is skipped otherwise. Message #5 shows the non-parallel-aware case cannot be handled today, and a committer asked for the extra callbacks. The proposal still does not say why ShutdownCustomScan is not enough for parallel-aware nodes.

Demand is thin but not absent. A committer who knows execParallel.c treats this as parity with the built-in scans, and only providers that implement the callbacks pay the cost, so the objection above asks for a real consumer and is not a call to reject.
